title: Spain's cultural participation has recovered broadly, but access is now a hybrid physical-platform system
source_unit: Spain Ministry of Culture Survey of Cultural Habits and Practices 2024-2025
geography: Spain; population aged 15 years and above

observations.period: 2024-2025 survey; annual and monthly cultural participation

denominator.unit: thousand people aged 15 years and above

read_any_book.unit: percent reading at least one book in the previous year

read_for_nonprofessional_reasons.unit: percent reading for reasons unrelated to profession or study in the previous year

museum_exhibition_gallery_visit.unit: percent visiting a museum, exhibition, or art gallery in the previous year

live_cultural_event.unit: percent attending a live cultural performance in the previous year

cinema.unit: percent attending cinema in the previous year

mechanism.value: Cultural participation is broad across reading, institutional visits, live events, and cinema rather than concentrated in one channel

observations.method: Ministry of Culture survey estimates for the population aged 15 and above; annual measures refer to the preceding year and monthly measures to the preceding month.
observations.uncertainty: The descriptive rates do not identify household spending, frequency beyond the reported period, causal drivers, or whether recovery reflects pent-up demand, cohort change, supply, or post-COVID normalization.
observations.subgroup: Total population aged 15 years and above in Spain.
observations.counterinterpretation: Annual participation can include one-off activity and therefore should not be treated as a measure of sustained cultural intensity or recurring willingness to pay.

observations.period: 2024-2025 survey; physical and digital reading/library access

denominator.unit: thousand people aged 15 years and above

paper_book.unit: percent reading at least one book in paper format in the previous year

digital_or_audiobook.unit: percent reading at least one book in digital format or audiobook in the previous year

direct_internet_reading.unit: percent reading books directly on the Internet in the previous year

library_any_access.unit: percent visiting or accessing a library virtually in the previous year

physical_library.unit: percent visiting a library in person in the previous year

online_library.unit: percent accessing a library through the Internet in the previous year

mechanism.value: Digital access is layered onto, rather than replacing, physical cultural infrastructure; the measures are not mutually exclusive

observations.method: Survey indicators distinguish paper, digital or audiobook reading, direct Internet reading, in-person library visits, and Internet library access; categories can overlap.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not establish paid versus free access, subscription duration, device constraints, title availability, or whether digital and physical users are the same people.
observations.subgroup: Total population aged 15 years and above in Spain.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital formats may expand access for some users while increasing costs, platform dependence, or discoverability barriers for others; overlap prevents a substitution claim.

observations.period: 2024-2025 survey; platform subscriptions and participation gaps by sex

denominator.unit: thousand people aged 15 years and above

any_digital_platform_subscription.unit: percent with a household subscription to at least one digital platform

film_or_series_platform.unit: percent with a household subscription to film or series platforms

music_platform.unit: percent with a household subscription to music platforms

book_or_audiobook_platform.unit: percent with a household subscription to book or audiobook platforms

monthly_audiovisual.unit: percent viewing audiovisual content in the previous month

monthly_music.unit: percent listening to music in the previous month

women_book_reading.unit: percent of women reading a book in the previous year

men_book_reading.unit: percent of men reading a book in the previous year

women_video_games.unit: percent of women playing video games in the previous month

men_video_games.unit: percent of men playing video games in the previous month

mechanism.value: Household cultural access is increasingly platform-mediated, but platform uptake and cultural practice remain differentiated by content type and gender

observations.method: Survey estimates combine household subscription indicators with individual cultural-practice measures; subscription categories and practice categories are not direct conversion measures.
observations.uncertainty: A household subscription does not reveal individual use, payment burden, account sharing, catalog quality, or whether the platform displaced physical consumption; sex differences are descriptive.
observations.subgroup: Total population aged 15 years and above, with sex-specific estimates for reading and video-game use.
observations.counterinterpretation: Platform subscriptions may coexist with free, pirated, public, or in-person access, and the gender differences may reflect age, life stage, social norms, or content preferences rather than platform exclusion.

related_sources.claim: The Ministry of Culture's official results hub identifies the survey as a national cultural-statistics operation and provides the 2024-2025 results.
Spain's National Statistics Institute inventory confirms the survey population aged 15 and above and its biennial statistical-program status.

boundary: This record adds Spain's official cultural-participation evidence with recovery, physical-digital overlap, platform subscription, and sex-differentiated practice signals. It does not estimate causal effects of platformization, household affordability, frequency intensity beyond the reported windows, or equivalence with Mexico's redesigned MODECULT population and instrument.
